title: High-performance protective-layer-free back-channel-etched praseodymium-doped ITZO thin-film transistors fabricated with PANs
content: The acid sensitivity of metal oxide semiconductors (MOS), such as IGZO, has hindered the mass production of back-channel-etched (BCE) MOS thin-film transistors (TFTs). In this work, we fabricated high-performance BCE praseodymium-doped indium tin zinc oxide (PITZO) TFTs without any channel-protective step. The PITZO thin films exhibited excellent acid resistance, as confirmed by microscopic inspection, etch-rate measurements, and surface-roughness tests. Therefore, the S/D electrodes could be patterned directly on the PITZO channel layer by a wet etching process, significantly lowering fabrication costs. Moreover, the PANs-processed devices exhibited superior performance with a threshold voltage (Vth) of 0.1 V, a saturation mobility of 23.8 cm2 V−1 s−1, and a subthreshold swing of 0.3 V per decade, while maintaining excellent bias-stress stability with a Vth shift of only 0.1 V under positive-bias temperature stress (PBTS) and −0.3 V under negative-bias illumination temperature stress (NBITS). As evidenced by trap density and XPS spectra analysis, PANs caused milder damage to the PITZO channel, while H2O2-based solution etching produced pronounced interface states that enhanced carrier scattering and trap capture. These findings demonstrate that PANs is a viable, high-performance S/D electrode etchant for BCE PITZO TFTs, which is not achievable for BCE IGZO TFTs. Overall, the paper offers a cost-effective route to address a fabrication bottleneck of BCE MOS TFTs, which could accelerate commercialisation.
